slides.subtitle: Evidence-led owner and AI-lab briefing · 1 October 2026
slides.title: RMS estate & language intelligence

slides.kicker: The answer in brief · R03/R04
scqa: The authorised staged subset contains 529.34 audio hours and 3,958 files. A separate transcript build contains 157,513 natural text units. These are candidate inventories, not an estate-wide qualified total.
Language-folder labels do not prove linguistic purity. Music exclusion, independent quality distributions, audio–text alignment and onward rights remain unresolved.
What should be protected, qualified and productised—and what can responsibly be offered to an AI lab?

Treat estate stewardship, corpus qualification and product development as separate workstreams. Pilot controlled-access products while building a defensible data card; do not sell a storage total as training-ready language data.
slides.title: The estate has valuable language assets, but its eligible corpus is not yet certified

slides.kicker: How to read this report · R07
points: Measured, estimated, proposed and unknown are different evidence classes.
Each number has a named population; database rows are not text examples.
File duration is not speech-only duration; unknown is not zero.
Storage units and snapshot dates are explicit throughout.
slides.title: The accounting rules prevent a large inventory from becoming an inflated AI claim
Estate intelligence: condition, duplication and stewardship

exhibit.label: Listed storage by separate inventory; not additive unique content
exhibit.receipt_text: OBS and NAS retained listings embedded in the census; 29 September 2026. Metadata scope, not language or music analysis.
exhibit.so_what: These are separate storage inventories. Overlap is unresolved; no unique-estate total is asserted.

slides.kicker: Part I · The estate is three overlapping inventories, not one clean corpus · R01/R02
slides.title: Most observed storage is media infrastructure, not a qualified language corpus

slides.kicker: Coverage is substantial but not complete or perfectly reconciled · R01/R02
points: Relational methods mix full reads, stratified samples and head samples.
OBS: 66 of 106 sources completed; 40 blocked or missing.
NAS: 16 of 16 registered roots enumerated; content qualification is separate.
Method counts and failure flags need reconciliation before statistical certification.
slides.title: Access coverage and content coverage must be reported separately

exhibit.label: Readiness grades of measured relational-table entries only
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS estate census, eij-1b359b3cbd2e; measured 29 September 2026. Exact source hashes in the Word appendix.
exhibit.so_what: The grades describe relational stewardship only; they do not classify speech quality, transcript accuracy or legal eligibility.

slides.kicker: Relational readiness is uneven and is not an audio-quality assessment · R01
slides.title: The readiness grades prioritise remediation; they do not certify a training dataset

slides.kicker: Quality and privacy signals are material, but their denominators differ · R01
points: Null-bearing is not the same as missing a mandatory field.
PII markers are a risk-screening signal, not a legal determination.
Degradation and stale-byte measures overlap; do not sum them.
Audio and transcript quality need their own independent measurements.
slides.title: The measured warning signals justify targeted inspection, not blanket rejection

slides.kicker: Duplication has several meanings and several confidence levels · R01/R04
points: Exact, normalised, sketch-near and semantic overlap are not interchangeable.
Relational candidates and transcript-cleaning counts are different populations.
Retain a canonical asset and lineage before retiring any copy.
Use identity controls to protect evaluation independence as well as storage.
slides.title: Duplicate candidates are an investigation queue, not a deletion instruction

slides.kicker: Object-store overlap and archive candidates offer leverage with qualifications · R02
points: 1.14 million object candidates are flagged by ETag and size, not universal hashes.
46.054 TB of old-write storage is an archive candidate, not proven unused.
Read demand, restore time, retrieval fees and retention must be checked.
Identity validation and reversible pilots precede reclamation.
slides.title: Archive and duplicate candidates are substantial, but net savings are not yet proven

slides.kicker: Freshness and growth need field-level interpretation · R01
points: Selected timestamps can represent events rather than writes.
Future dates and sentinel values need explicit treatment.
Storage deltas are not automatically business growth rates.
Freshness must be defined for each intended product.
slides.title: Freshness is a product-specific property, not a universal timestamp rule

slides.kicker: Storage economics should be quoted as conditional bounds · R01/R02/R07
points: Use the owner’s effective tariff and actual billing units.
Gross standard-tier cost is not net archive savings.
Do not add overlapping reclamation and tiering opportunities.
Model restore, egress, retention and migration costs explicitly.
slides.title: The economics are useful bounds, not an invoice-backed savings commitment

slides.kicker: Stewardship priorities should protect value before removing cost · R07
points: Establish ownership and canonical identity first.
Validate read workloads and restore obligations before tiering.
Review index candidates against real queries, not schema shape alone.
Run corpus qualification alongside—not behind—the entire cleanup programme.
slides.title: Stewardship and corpus qualification can proceed together without conflating their goals
Non-English, non-music audio and text: a defensible accounting

slides.kicker: Part II · The precise answer is a bounded candidate inventory · R03/R04
points: 529.34 staged audio hours; 36.52 GB; music and language purity unverified.
157,513 natural text units; 27.33 million characters; separate source population.
Estate-wide eligible totals and quality distributions remain unmeasured.
The uncertainty is a qualification gap, not evidence that suitable data is absent.
slides.title: The verified inventory is sizeable; the strictly eligible total remains unknown

exhibit.label: Measured staged-audio duration by folder label, not certified speech hours
exhibit.receipt_text: Staged-audio header inspection, m9j-3e0dcb1bd16e; verified receipt. Folder labels are not content verification.
exhibit.so_what: Folder labels are provisional linguistic metadata; file duration is not isolated speech time.

slides.kicker: The audio-duration distribution is highly uneven · R03/R04
slides.title: The smallest audio strata need deliberate qualification, not pooled reporting

exhibit.label: Staged-audio file counts by sample rate; not a quality grade
exhibit.receipt_text: Staged-audio header inspection, m9j-3e0dcb1bd16e; verified receipt. Folder labels are not content verification.
exhibit.so_what: Sample rate and readable headers are observed properties, not a measured clean-speech distribution.

slides.kicker: Capture properties are measurable; quality grades are not yet established · R03
slides.title: The evidence describes capture formats, not yet the quality of usable speech

slides.kicker: The waveform measurement record is incomplete and stale · R06
points: The retained progress counter is not a completed measurement dataset.
Its stale heartbeat cannot establish current remote process health.
No completed quality-band percentages are defensible from that record.
Finish and reconcile the measurement receipt before publishing distributions.
slides.title: A stale progress record cannot stand in for a completed quality measurement

slides.kicker: Define non-English and non-music at the segment level · R07
points: Count segments, not entire programmes, for strict eligibility.
Separate English-only, code-switched and local-language-only speech.
Separate music-only and speech-with-music; keep unresolved content explicit.
Agree the recipient’s acceptance definition before producing the final quantity.
slides.title: The target corpus is an intersection of verified properties, not a folder selection

exhibit.label: Natural assembled text units by language label
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS transcript assembly, m9j-9a46b862f339; sealed 29 September 2026. Natural units exclude added canaries.
exhibit.so_what: The text-unit inventory is verified within this build; token mass and alignment require their own definitions.

slides.kicker: Text quantity is real, but units, characters and tokens are different · R04/R05
slides.title: Text units establish a corpus inventory, not a universal token or speech equivalent

exhibit.label: Natural text partition counts; added synthetic canaries excluded
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS transcript assembly, m9j-9a46b862f339; sealed 29 September 2026. Natural units exclude added canaries.
exhibit.so_what: Partition integrity, speaker independence and final-evaluation blindness are separate requirements.

slides.kicker: The existing partitions provide useful structure, not final independence proof · R04
slides.title: A sealed evaluation file is not automatically an untouched final benchmark

slides.kicker: Transcript quality and aligned speech hours are still open · R03/R04/R07
points: WER/CER and clean paired hours are not measured in the current record.
Language-ID accuracy does not validate every transcript.
Audio–text joins need timestamps, hashes, provenance and rights.
Qualify by intended task rather than inventing a single “good data” grade.
slides.title: The transcript corpus is promising, but supervised-speech quality is not yet quantified

slides.kicker: The text model proves a narrow capability, not corpus-wide quality · R05
points: The held-out evaluation presents 400 examples per language; 2,800 in total. Conditional macro accuracy is 97.213%.
Kikamba: 91.349% conditional accuracy; 98.25% coverage; 89.75% correct across all presented examples.
Kiswahili: 98.950% conditional accuracy; 95.25% coverage; 94.25% correct across all presented examples.
This measures language identification—not ASR fidelity, general reasoning, linguistic purity or data rights.
slides.title: The admitted text classifier validates one task; it does not certify the whole estate

slides.kicker: Compute eligible hours with an auditable segment ledger · R07
points: Eligible hours are the duration-weighted intersection of explicit gates.
Separate included, excluded and unresolved duration.
Stratify by language, source, time, programme and acoustic condition.
Use design-aware uncertainty; do not multiply marginal percentages.
slides.title: An auditable ledger can turn the candidate inventory into a credible lab offer

slides.kicker: A sampling illustration is not a substitute for the actual design · R07
points: Illustrative sample formulas assume independence and a defined population.
Correlated recordings and rare strata change the effective sample size.
No detected contamination is not proof of zero contamination.
Tolerance, adjudication and release policy must be agreed explicitly.
slides.title: The qualification design should expose uncertainty rather than hide it

slides.kicker: What a global AI lab should receive · R07/R08
points: A data card, manifest and rights matrix must travel with the corpus.
Provide per-stratum quality, uncertainty and failure counts—not one pooled score.
Supply independently reproducible partitions and evaluation evidence.
Offer controlled qualification before promising unrestricted licensing.
slides.title: A lab-ready offer is a reproducible evidence package, not a storage statistic
A broader portfolio: commercial services and local-language enablement

slides.kicker: Part III · Data value depends on the product and the permitted use · R07
points: Enterprise services, research products and ecosystem investment have different economics.
Start with a narrow qualified slice and a named user problem.
Do not equate an attractive use case with present eligibility.
Validate willingness to pay before treating the portfolio as revenue.
slides.title: The estate supports several product hypotheses—not one undifferentiated data sale

slides.kicker: Context as a service · R07
points: Offer: Versioned, cited retrieval of authorised local context through a governed interface; language routing, provenance, freshness and correction are part of the product.
Users: Enterprise assistants, newsrooms, research teams and approved local-language applications.
Value model: Subscription, usage or enterprise agreement; validate retention, citation utility, answer coverage and workflow savings.
Gate: Source rights for retrieval and excerpting; publication updates; factual review; privacy and content-access boundaries.
slides.title: Cited context can support bounded enterprise workflows

slides.kicker: Local-language transcription, captions and media accessibility · R07
points: Offer: Task-specific ASR, captions, alignment and searchable timecodes for qualified language/acoustic strata.
Users: Broadcasters, archives, public-service content teams and accessibility programmes.
Value model: Per-minute processing, managed service or enterprise contract; quality-linked acceptance and rework costs determine margin.
Gate: Clean paired segments, independently checked references, lawful processing and a supported rather than assumed model capability.
slides.title: Transcription services require validated speech–text alignment

slides.kicker: Independent local-language benchmark and evaluation service · R07
points: Offer: A controlled, blind benchmark with per-language/dialect scoring, abstention and coverage, leakage checks and human adjudication.
Users: Model developers, global AI labs and local-language application buyers.
Value model: Evaluation engagements, secure benchmark access or recurring independent assessments.
Gate: Independent labels and partitions; benchmark rights; conflict-of-interest controls. The current language-ID score alone is not a benchmark product.
slides.title: Independent evaluation can turn language coverage into a service

slides.kicker: Rights-cleared research corpus licensing · R07
points: Offer: Versioned corpus slices with a data card, manifest, permissible-use terms, correction/withdrawal process and documented quality.
Users: AI labs and research institutions with a defined training or evaluation objective.
Value model: Scoped licence, time-bound access, support or recurring updates, subject to actual rights and demonstrated buyer need.
Gate: Onward-use rights, contributor and programme permissions, privacy review, geographic transfer terms and verified quality. Not cleared by internal training authorisation alone.
slides.title: Corpus licensing is a rights-and-assurance product, not a raw data sale

slides.kicker: Secure research enclave and compute-to-data access · R07
points: Offer: Approved code executes against a controlled dataset slice; reviewed metrics and permitted outputs leave the environment.
Users: Research partners unable to receive unrestricted source copies.
Value model: Project access, managed research environment or jointly funded programme.
Gate: Approved partner and purpose, adequate controls, contractual liability and a qualified dataset. This is not a loophole around data-protection law.
slides.title: Compute-to-data access limits raw-data movement, not the underlying obligations

slides.kicker: Open-source local-language enablement and heritage access · R07
points: Offer: Open tools, schemas, evaluation harnesses and documentation; separately approved dataset or model releases where rights allow.
Users: Local researchers, universities, developers and language communities.
Value model: Grant or consortium support, sponsorship, hosted/support services and partnership adoption; open-source itself is not a guaranteed revenue stream.
Gate: Licence compatibility, release-specific rights, community stewardship, hosting support and an explicit sustainability plan.
slides.title: Open-source tools can build an ecosystem without premature corpus release

slides.kicker: The wider portfolio extends beyond corpus sales and context APIs · R07
points: Private archive search and terminology resources can build on smaller curated slices.
Localisation and adapters need task-specific evidence, not broad model claims.
Annotation and independent evaluation improve the defensibility of later offers.
Voice synthesis and unmarked synthetic augmentation are not shortcuts around rights.
slides.title: The strongest portfolio combines services, assurance and local-language capability

slides.kicker: Context as a service needs a product contract, not just a vector index · R07
points: Define domains, languages, freshness, citation and abstention behaviour.
Carry source permissions into retrieval, caches and generated answers.
Evaluate faithful answers separately from retrieval relevance.
Price the full cost of an accepted answer, including curation and escalation.
slides.title: A defensible context service sells trustworthy workflow support, not raw retrieval

slides.kicker: An open ecosystem and a commercial service can coexist · R07/R08
points: Open code, open data, open weights and a hosted service are different choices.
Start with reproducible tools and clear documentation; clear data separately.
Native-speaker participation and correction channels are part of the product.
Assign funding and ownership for maintenance, not just launch.
slides.title: Openness is a set of deliberate release decisions, not a single licence label

slides.kicker: Rights, privacy and community legitimacy constrain the offer · R08/R07
points: Internal authorisation does not establish onward licensing or open-release rights.
Assess source, performer, transcript, personal-data and derived-output rights separately.
Cross-border processing requires a documented legal and operational review.
Community participation and correction rights strengthen long-term legitimacy.
slides.title: Rights and stewardship must be designed into each offer, not appended at release

slides.kicker: Commercial validation should precede a revenue forecast · R07
points: Validate a named buyer problem and acceptance criteria in a scoped pilot.
Use accepted outputs—not raw gigabytes—as the economic unit.
Include rights, annotation, review, maintenance and support costs.
No revenue forecast is justified before yield, demand and delivery costs are measured.
slides.title: A paid qualification or workflow pilot is stronger evidence than a speculative valuation

slides.kicker: A staged programme turns the inventory into a responsible offer · R07
points: Establish source identity, coverage and rights before a sale claim.
Qualify segments and alignments with independent native-speaker evidence.
Pilot one bounded commercial workflow and a separately cleared open track.
Scale only after measured quality, demand, correction and unit economics are credible.
slides.title: The next investment should buy qualification and a pilot, not a larger unverified claim

slides.kicker: Decisions for the owner and prospective partner · R07
points: Select the intended use, target strata and release model.
Agree treatment of mixed content and unresolved quality.
Name accountable owners for rights, language validation and delivery.
Approve the qualification programme and a bounded pilot—not unsupported totals.
slides.title: The next decision is the first defensible product and its qualification contract
